mainText:
Paul Thompson is to leave as RNZ chief executive six weeks early, with news boss Mark Stevens stepping up as acting chief from Tuesday, as the broadcaster deals with an eleven point eight million dollar financial blowout. Here is today's news.

New Zealand.

RNZ chief executive Paul Thompson will leave on Monday, more than six weeks ahead of schedule, following the overspend and a disputed five million dollar overdraft. Head of News Mark Stevens becomes acting chief executive from Tuesday. Former board member Jane Wrightson says she knew ministerial approval was needed for the overdraft but does not know why it was never sought. A review is expected to report most findings before Christmas.

Coalition talks continue with the final vote count still weeks away. An explainer doing the rounds covers what happens if the overhang leaves Parliament unable to agree on a government. Former Prime Minister Sir Geoffrey Palmer has called the current seat overhang constitutionally sad and says it should be brought to a halt. Negotiations can start now, an expert says, regardless of the twenty day wait for final numbers.

Thousands of students face a derived grades process after the NCEA English exam platform failed again this week, the second straight day of outages. Students switched to paper copies and NZQA's chief has fronted publicly on the fix.

Microsoft says recovery from its global outage is continuing, with Outlook, Teams and Copilot returning after nearly twenty four hours of disruption. New Zealand police, councils and Air New Zealand were among those hit. Microsoft says the cause was a technical fault, not a cyber or AI issue.

In the Bay of Plenty, the byelection triggered by Western Bay of Plenty councillor Alan Kurtovich's resignation continues, with Kurtovich confirming the Māori wards vote was the reason he quit. A man who stabbed a friend to death after a party has had his manslaughter sentence reduced and may serve as little as two years.

World.

Nvidia's crisis has widened beyond Jensen Huang's resignation. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has blamed the Commerce Department for failing to block chip sales to Megaspeed, a firm reported to have traded more than four billion US dollars of Nvidia chips in two years. Huang has been summoned to testify before Congress over his affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. Donald Trump has suggested Apple's Tim Cook should replace him. Chief financial officer Colette Kress remains interim chief executive while the board searches for a permanent successor.

United States flights were grounded nationwide after what officials called extraordinary circumstances hitting all air traffic control centres, Transport Secretary Sean Duffy said. Disruption followed a day after the separate Microsoft outage, which also hit Britain's National Health Service, schools and police forces, and continues into a second day for some services.

London's Metropolitan Police are investigating comedian and children's author David Walliams over allegations of serious sexual offences, separate to earlier reports from other broadcasters. In the United States, a tanker struck a river cruise boat carrying one hundred and twenty nine passengers in New Orleans on Friday, partially submerging it, with rescues underway.

Technology.

Microsoft has apologised, calling its outage a stark reminder of global reliance on a small number of big technology providers. The company says elevated server load triggered cascading failures across Outlook, Teams and Copilot, with recovery still being completed almost a full day later. Governments, hospitals and intelligence services from the United States to Australia reported disruption.

The FBI says North Korean hackers used fake video calls to steal around four hundred million US dollars in cryptocurrency, in a scheme called FaceStealer that has caught more than nine hundred victims over eighteen months. Investigators say the hackers impersonated contacts on video calls to gain access to victims' systems before draining funds.

Sport.

League. The Kiwis and Kiwi Ferns meet the Kangaroos and Jillaroos in the Rugby League World Cup finals in Brisbane. Kalyn Ponga and Stacey Waaka have already been named International Rugby League Players of the Year. Briton Nikora, who once worked scaffolding jobs, starts for the Kiwis in the final as one of the game's leading back rowers.

Cricket. The Black Caps crushed India in the fourth One Day International at Mount Maunganui, Young scoring a century and Henry taking six wickets, setting a target of three hundred and thirty four. New Zealand won by two hundred and forty four runs, India's second worst ODI defeat, keeping the series alive.

Formula One. Liam Lawson has been confirmed at Racing Bulls for twenty twenty seven. Analysts say he cannot afford to relax this week if he wants a long term seat on the grid.

Football. The All Whites beat India in a rare fixture between the two nations. Coach Darren Bazeley says the winning margin should have been greater given the chances created.

Football. Manchester United have appointed Mauricio Pochettino as manager, ahead of their November twenty second match against Liverpool. Pochettino becomes United's eighth permanent manager since Alex Ferguson retired in twenty thirteen, having left the United States national job to take the role.

Basketball. The Breakers snapped a five game losing streak with an overtime win over Brisbane. DJ Vasiljevic scored thirty six points and Carlin Davison recorded a triple double.

Coming up. The Rugby League World Cup finals continue in Brisbane this weekend. Coalition talks continue in Wellington with the final vote count still weeks away. Christopher Luxon will attend the Asia-Pacific summit in China next week in a caretaker capacity.

End of flash.
